Commentary.Commentary: It is going to be interesting last few overs of the day. Stay tuned as the third innings is about to begin.
Sri Lanka would like to complete a whitewash over the visitors and would come out to bat in that fashion.

Earlier in the innings, Shaun Marsh and Steven Smith went on to make centuries, which got the visitors going as they went on to make a humongous 246-run partnership. They now lead by 24 runs. The home side will firstly have to see off Starc and Co. without losing any wickets and then build up on their start tomorrow. Because it will be difficult for Australia to chase a big total on the 5th day against Herath and company in this sort of form.

Sri Lanka whizzed through the Australian lower order. Adam Voges departed soon after the Tea break. After that Mitchell Marsh-Peter Nevill stand steadied the Australian ship which helped them go past Sri Lanka's first innings total with the former completing his half-century. Herath once again proved to be the wrecker-in-chief picking up 6 wickets. He was well supported by Dilruwan Perera who picked up 2 wickets.

The ball goes and deflects off Kusal's gloves to the right of Mathews at first slip, who does a good job to gobble it. Australia bowled out at 379 and they lead by 24 runs.

Talking about the hosts and their bowling, they weren't a threat at all. Apart from a dropped catch early in the morning session, they didn't look penetrative enough to create a breakthrough. The spin duo of Herath and Perera was dealt with ease and so was Sandakan. The Sri Lankan side needs to buck up and bowl better after the break to stop the Australian charge. Do join us in a bit for the post-Lunch session.

The Australian side takes another session in their kitty. From being on 141/1 at the start of day's play to 235/1 at lunch, they are only 120 runs behind the Lankan's total now. Marsh and Smith have certainly converted their starts into centuries and are amidst a record double century stand at the moment.  They were determined to play their strokes but were watchful at the same time as well.

Russel Arnold says just pitching in good areas and hope that the pitch does the magic is not going to work for Sri Lanka. They will have to work harder. It is going to be more of a mental battle for both the sides. Fitness will be one of the important factors as it is a very hot and humid day. He ends up saying that the players will have to fight the demons in their head because they aren't any present on the pitch.

The hosts will have to pull up their socks with the ball this morning as the Aussies are looking determined and have played spin bowling better. It promises to be yet another cracking day of Test cricket.

Hello and warm welcome for day 3 of the third Test between Sri Lanka and Australia at Colombo. The visiting side has shown a great comeback on day 2 with a team total of 141/1. The skipper has led from the front with his fifty alongside an able partner in Shaun Marsh who has also scored an unbeaten fifty. The duo is at the crease with a partnership of 120 and will look to go strength to strength to lessen the deficit of 200 plus runs.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

Australia batted superbly today but then that's past now and they will have to start fresh again tomorrow morning. The deficit is still in excess of 200 and they cannot afford to relax. The Aussies will hope for the current partnership to prosper and bat for as long as possible. Sri Lanka on the other hand will try harder on Day 3 and will wish for more assistance from the pitch. Do join us at 1000 IST for all the action. Cheers!

Sri Lanka bowled well but have to say that the Australian batsmen batted better. Apart from a few deliveries misbehaving here and there and a couple chances going down, there wasn't much to trouble the Aussies. A lot of credit should be given to Steven Smith and Shaun Marsh for the way they dealt with the Lankan spinners. Also for the first time in this series, Australia have two batsmen scoring fifties in an innings and this has provided them a solid beginning.

Finally a fightback by Australia with the bat in the series! It didn't start well for them when they lost David Warner cheaply but then the pair of Smith and Marsh batted sensibly against the Sri Lankan spinners to form a partnership. A stand which is worth 120 runs at the moment, only the second 50-plus stand for the visitors in the series.

Stay tuned as we have an action packed session to follow as the Sri Lankan bowlers would look to hunt down the Aussie batters. While the latter would looks to fight them back with a spirited performance with the bat which they have lacked this series. Third session to follow...

Australia came in to bat and was served a juicy full toss first up. But suffered again as they lost Warner within the first few overs. Now, Smith and Marsh are out in the middle and will look to stay as long as possible. Sri Lanka even without their main man Herath out injured produced a break through de Silva and would be overly joyous with the this.

83 runs scored for the loss of 3 wickets in this session! This session also was dominated by the home side. Post lunch Sri Lanka came in and scored 56 runs with the help from a partnership from Chandimal and Herath. Chandimal fell in the process to up the run rate. As soon as he fell, so did the tail. OUT! Warner is caught behind! Big setback for Australia and once again he departs after looking good in the middle. A flatter delivery, around off and skidding in, it's a bit on the shorter side too, Warner pushes his weight on the back foot, tries to cut but gets a inside edge behind to the keeper. Perera wearing the gloves shows great reflexes to catch the ball. They appeal and the finger goes up. Warner stands back in surprise for a while and then walks back. He had the option of of reviewing it but it seems that he realized about the edge a little late. Anyway, Australia lose Warner cheaply and are off to a poor start yet again.
